newsitem.title: UK: OECD end-Sept industry oil stocks 91 mln barrels.
newsitem.headline: OECD end-Sept industry oil stocks 91 mln barrels.

text.p: End-September industry oil stocks held by OECD member countries stood a sharp 91 million barrels below the same period 1995 with distillates making up more than half the shortfall, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
In its end-October Monthly Oil Market Report, the Paris-based IEA said OECD oil inventories rose a slim 0.1 million bpd in September and averaged just 0.4 million in the third quarter.
But the stock shortfall is expected to "decrease appreciably" in the fourth quarter, the agency said.
It expected the stock tightness to ease largely because of a bullish forecast for non-OPEC supply and and due to the "historically high stockdraw" of 1.2 million bpd in the fourth qaurter 1995.
The IEA expects non-OPEC supply to increase to 45 million bpd in the fourth quarter, 1.8 million from third quarter 1996 and a massive 2.3 million bpd from fourth quarter 1995.
At the end of September, 49 million barrels of the total year-on-year decline was of distillates, the IEA said.

Though distillate inventories in the OECD Pacific were up year-on-year, stock levels in the OECD Europe were down 14 percent from end-September 1995 and 10 percent down in North America, the agency said.
Total OECD industry stocks at the end of September were 2.429 billion barrels, 91 million below 1995 or about three days lower in terms of days of forward demand, the IEA said.

The IEA, the West's energy watchdog, said it made a "major" 48 million barrel downward revision to preliminary August stock data largely because of a 23 million barrel revision by the French government to the allocation of stocks between industry and government.
